title: Getting Projects Under Control
coreMove: Lift from next-action execution to project control by checking each project for a clear outcome, visible moving parts, and a next action.
sourcePressure: The chapter returns to project-level control after the daily ground game is reliable, using creative planning and project visibility without replaying the whole planning theory.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reopening every project as a grand planning exercise instead of using ground-level control to recover project visibility.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: ground game
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar links project control to reliable lower-level execution.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Project control comes back when the runway is clean enough to show which projects are still airborne.

sourceAnchors.name: creative planning
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar supports creative planning as part of returning to project-level thinking.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Creative planning is useful here only when it reconnects a stuck project to visible movement.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional blood-drive coordinator whose spring campaign has stalled
exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator managing donor sites, volunteers, and clinical partners
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed site confirmations could shrink the donor pool for the quarter
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The mobile cooler is already serviced when Olivia notices the campaign has no visible outcome, owner list, or next site call.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a mobile blood cooler with a fresh inspection sticker

exampleSpecs.domain: a board-game publisher preparing a delayed print run
exampleSpecs.audience: a production lead juggling art, factory proofs, and retailer dates
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed proof approval could push holiday delivery past its sales window
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 11:18 a.m., Ryan stops staring at "finish print run" and writes the outcome, three moving parts, and the next factory email.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a color proof strip beside a production calendar

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal tree-planting project after permit delays
exampleSpecs.audience: a parks planner recovering a project that drifted under daily work
exampleSpecs.stakes: saplings could arrive before permits, crews, or neighborhood notices are ready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Olivier one pallet of early saplings to see that the project existed as a name but not as controlled moving parts.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pallet tag tied to bare-root saplings

exampleSpecs.domain: an independent documentary editor reviving an unfinished grant cut
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative professional whose project has become emotional fog
exampleSpecs.stakes: the grant deadline could pass while the footage remains only partly sorted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What part of Anke’s film is actually uncontrolled: the story, the footage bins, or the missing next action?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hard drive labeled rough cut on a desk

exampleSpecs.domain: a university dining director fixing a reusable-container rollout
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations director whose daily fixes obscure project control
exampleSpecs.stakes: students may abandon the program if deposits, signage, and washing flow remain vague
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Steam rises from the dish line while Adaeze maps the outcome and separates signage, deposits, and wash flow into owned next actions.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam above a dish line with green containers stacked nearby

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth soccer league treasurer rebuilding a failed registration project
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer treasurer dealing with parents, insurance, and field permits
exampleSpecs.stakes: a season start date could slip because everyone thought someone else owned registration
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Who owns the next move?" Pablo asks, and the room gets quiet because the project was visible only as a shared worry.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stack of unsigned registration forms beside field permits

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: repair stuck projects without replaying all planning phases
connect project visibility to next-action lists

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one project and write three lines: desired outcome, current stuck point, next physical action owned by a real person.
